boards.title: Your First Weekend at Seton Hall University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A documented, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented on campus, trying an activity, and connecting with South Orange.

cards.title: Start with Pirate Adventure
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation activity
cards.notes: Use your orientation schedule to meet your peer group, complete required sessions, and ask where to find the next campus stop before heading out on your own.
cards.short_summary: Seton Hall identifies Pirate Adventure as its orientation program for all first-year students.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall’s current acceptance packet identifies Pirate Adventure as the new-student orientation program for all first-year students.
cards.access_notes: Follow the orientation schedule and any registration instructions provided to new students.

cards.title: Pause at the campus chapel
cards.subtitle: Seton Hall’s spiritual center
cards.notes: Step inside during an open service period or take a quiet look at the restored chapel; check Campus Ministry’s schedule before planning a visit.
cards.short_summary: The 1863 chapel is a prominent historic campus destination with regularly scheduled Masses.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall describes the Chapel of the Immaculate Conception as the spiritual center of campus, built in 1863 and renovated in 2008.
cards.access_notes: Mass is offered multiple times daily; consult Campus Ministry for the current worship schedule.

cards.title: Set up at Walsh Library
cards.subtitle: Second-floor Information Commons
cards.notes: Find the second-floor commons, test your account on a workstation, and note the printers and scanners so routine academic tasks feel familiar next week.
cards.short_summary: A practical first study stop with student-accessible computers, printers, scanners, and accessibility technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walsh Library Information Commons is on the second floor and provides 55 desktop computers, printers, scanners, and an adaptive-technology workstation.
cards.access_notes: General use is open to the Seton Hall community; lab hours correspond to Walsh Library hours.

cards.title: Check the University Theatre schedule
cards.subtitle: Bishop Dougherty University Center
cards.notes: Look for the next mainstage listing, then decide whether to attend, audition, or ask Theatre Council how to participate behind the scenes.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus performance space where Seton Hall presents theatre and invites students of any major to audition.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall Theatre says the University Theatre is in the University Center and that any student, regardless of major, may audition for mainstage shows.
cards.access_notes: Check the production schedule; Seton Hall Theatre states that admission to its productions is always free.

cards.entity_name: Richie Regan Recreation and Athletic Center
cards.title: Take a lap through the Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Fitness center and recreation facilities
cards.notes: Bring your student ID, locate the fitness-center entrance, and choose a low-key first workout or ask staff about classes, intramurals, and club sports.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation destination with fitness equipment, studios, locker rooms, and pool access.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall says the Richie Regan Recreation and Athletic Center has a two-floor fitness center, cardio stations, dance studios, weight training, locker rooms, and access to the natatorium.
cards.source_title: Richie Regan Recreation and Athletic Center
cards.access_notes: During the academic year, the field house and fitness center list weekend hours of 9 a.m.–7 p.m.; schedules can change.

cards.title: See Pirate Radio in action
cards.subtitle: WSOU studios in the Richie Regan Recreation and Athletic Center
cards.notes: Visit the station location and contact its manager if broadcasting, production, sports, news, or promotion sounds appealing—participation is open across majors.
cards.short_summary: Seton Hall’s student-operated radio station offers hands-on roles from hosting to engineering.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall states that WSOU 89.5 FM is operated by student managers, offers multiple student staff roles, and is open to students across the University’s programs.
cards.access_notes: WSOU is located in the Richie Regan Recreation and Athletic Center; contact the station manager before arranging a visit or joining.

cards.title: Ride the SHU Fly loop
cards.subtitle: Campus and South Orange Village transportation
cards.notes: Use the published schedule and map to make one daylight loop through South Orange Village, then save the stops that make future errands and outings simpler.
cards.short_summary: A student-ID shuttle loop linking campus and South Orange Village at no charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall says SHU Fly runs a loop from campus through South Orange Village and is free for students with ID.
cards.access_notes: Seton Hall says the loop runs from early morning until after the last NYC train arrives; consult its current schedules and maps.

cards.title: Find SOPAC downtown
cards.subtitle: One SOPAC Way, South Orange
cards.notes: Use the SHU Fly map or walk with a group in daylight to locate SOPAC, then review the calendar for a future Seton Hall Theatre performance.
cards.short_summary: A downtown South Orange performance venue used by Seton Hall Theatre for mainstage work.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall Theatre identifies SOPAC at One SOPAC Way in South Orange as one of its two performance locations.
cards.access_notes: Seton Hall Theatre recommends registration for its performances at SOPAC; review the event listing before going.

cards.title: Locate Owen T. Carroll Field
cards.subtitle: Home field for Seton Hall soccer
cards.notes: Walk over to identify the field and seating area, then check the official athletics schedule before returning for a soccer match or campus event.
cards.short_summary: A renovated campus athletics venue associated with both Seton Hall soccer programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall Athletics identifies Owen T. Carroll Field as the renovated home of its men’s and women’s soccer teams.
cards.access_notes: Check the official athletics schedule and event-specific entry information before attending a match.

cards.title: Bookmark a DOVE service option
cards.subtitle: Campus Ministry volunteer programs
cards.notes: Browse the weekly opportunities, pick one cause that fits your schedule, and contact DOVE for the registration steps instead of arriving unannounced at a partner site.
cards.short_summary: DOVE coordinates recurring volunteer projects and service-learning opportunities for Seton Hall students.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall says DOVE coordinates projects, trips, and initiatives, including weekly visits to a local soup kitchen, and directs students to its volunteer opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Review DOVE’s current weekly opportunities and registration requirements before committing to a project.
